theme: The Son of Man; the four beasts
readingInstruction: Read Daniel 7:1-8:27. The second half of Daniel begins with visions. Four beasts rise from the sea, and one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven. Read chapter 7 slowly, especially verses 9 to 14. This is one of the most important passages in the Bible.
settingTheScene: The visions of Daniel 7 and 8 date to about 553 and 551 BC, before the events of chapters 5 and 6, but they are placed here to open the apocalyptic part of the book. The visions use symbolic beasts to describe the empires of the earth. In chapter 7, which is in Aramaic, Daniel sees four beasts and then a heavenly courtroom. In chapter 8, he sees a ram and a goat, which many interpreters understand as Persia and Greece.
observation: “Four great beasts came up out of the sea, different from one another” (7:3).
“As I looked, thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days took his seat” (7:9).
“His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames” (7:9).
“A stream of fire issued and came out from before him” (7:10).
“Behold, with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man, and he came to the Ancient of Days and was presented before him” (7:13).
“And to him was given dominion and glory and a kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him” (7:14).
“His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom one that shall not be destroyed” (7:14).
“And the kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High” (7:27).
interpretation:
The four beasts are a lion with eagle’s wings, a bear raised on one side, a leopard with four heads, and a terrifying fourth beast with iron teeth and ten horns. They are usually understood as successive empires: Babylon, Persia, Greece, and Rome or a later power. They rise from the chaotic sea. The fourth has a little horn that speaks great things and wages war against the saints. The beasts show the nature of human empires: violent, devouring, and arrogant.

Then the scene shifts. Thrones are set, and the Ancient of Days takes his seat. The picture is of a heavenly court. His clothing is white as snow, and his throne is flames of fire with wheels of burning fire. Thousands upon thousands serve him. The books are opened. The beast is slain, and its body burned. The other beasts lose their dominion.

Then comes the climax: “With the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man.” Clouds are the vehicle of God in the Old Testament. This figure approaches the Ancient of Days and receives everlasting dominion over all peoples. The kingdoms of the beasts rise from the sea. The kingdom of the son of man comes from heaven. Beasts devour, but the son of man is given all authority.

Daniel is troubled by the vision. An attendant explains: the four beasts are four kings. “But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and possess the kingdom forever.” The Son of Man shares his rule with his people.

Chapter 8 is a second vision of a ram, a goat, and a little horn that desecrates the sanctuary. It looks beyond to the persecution under Antiochus Epiphanes in the second century BC, a type of later enemies. Daniel is overcome by the vision and falls sick. The consistent message: the powers of this world, however terrifying, are limited by God’s decree.
connection: Jesus called himself “the Son of Man” more than eighty times. At his trial, he said to the high priest, “You will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven” (Mark 14:62), and the high priest tore his robes, understanding the claim. Matthew 28:18: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.” Revelation 1:7, 13-14 shows him coming with the clouds, white-haired. Revelation 13 shows the beast, and Revelation 5 shows the Lamb receiving the kingdom.
application:
Spend time meditating on Daniel 7:13-14, and think about Jesus as the one to whom all dominion is given.

When world powers seem terrifying, remember that the Ancient of Days is on the throne and the books are open.

Pray for those who are persecuted, remembering that the kingdom will be given to the saints.
prayerPrompts: Thank him for the Son of Man whose kingdom will not pass away.
Ask him to give you courage in the meantime.
